conventions.convention: Modules used for induction and restriction are left modules; induction is H tensor over H_J with M, using H as a right H_J-module. Restricted-system parameters are inherited from the ambient system, even when distinct restricted odd-edge components share a parameter.

Right cosets are W_J d and left cosets are d W_J. D_R consists of elements with no left J-descent and supplies the left H_J-module basis; D_L consists of elements with no right J-descent and supplies the right H_J-module basis used for induction.

For finite W, the canonical trace extracts the coefficient of T_1. Perfectness means that a maps to the functional b maps to tau(ab) is an isomorphism over the coefficient ring, without a field or semisimplicity assumption.
The trace-dual vector to T_w is T indexed by w inverse, rather than the algebra inverse of T_w.

load_bearing.statement: Assume W is finite. For all x,y in W, tau(T_x T_y) = delta_(x inverse,y). Consequently the canonical trace is symmetric and its pairing map H to Hom_R(H,R) is an isomorphism. The inverse-indexed standard basis is trace-dual, and the same assertions hold after every unital homomorphism of commutative coefficient rings.

H_J is the embedded restricted-system Hecke algebra. H has left H_J-basis indexed by D_R(J) and right H_J-basis indexed by D_L(J), for possibly infinite W. If M has R-basis B, its induced module has R-basis consisting of T_d tensor b for d in D_L(J), b in B. The displayed evaluation and balanced-extension maps give the induction-restriction adjunction.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite generator-set convention, presented Coxeter group, length, reduced expressions and standard parabolic subgroup.
Universal Laurent coefficient ring, inherited odd-component parameters, quadratic normalization T_s squared equals 1 plus (v_s minus v_s inverse) T_s, and braid relations.
Well-defined reduced products and left/right multiplication rules used in parabolic closure and the trace-dual example.
Explicit length operators and reduced-product evaluation at e_1 used in the coordinate-transpose trace proof.
Standard-basis independence, length-operator representation, and preservation of the basis under arbitrary commutative base change.
Intrinsic restricted Coxeter presentation and length, unique minimal representatives on both sides, and additive parabolic factorizations.
Balanced tensor construction for a right module and a left module over a possibly noncommutative ring.
Descent of additive balanced maps defining induced-module actions and the explicit tensor maps.
Checking that gH denotes a left coset and Hg a right coset throughout the parabolic theorem and example.
Simple-submodule classification in the dual-number counterexample.
Semisimplicity as an internal direct sum of simple submodules in the counterexample.

concerns.concern: Proof step 1.1 says: 'Each T_u is a product of the generators indexed by J, so K_J contains the subalgebra they generate'. This premise instead proves that K_J is contained in the generated R-subalgebra. The next sentence supplies the other inclusion through closure under generators and containment of 1. The equality is supported by the argument, but the first containment is written in the wrong direction.

seams_checked.note: Checked both page interfaces and the downstream specialization/regular-trace definition. The downstream text explicitly distinguishes the regular-trace pairing from the preceding canonical symmetrizing pairing; it does not infer semisimplicity from canonical-trace perfectness. The supplier page likewise makes no field-semisimplicity assertion and provides an explicit nonsemisimple specialization.
